messages.content: i opened a book i read as a child. i still like it, but i think about the father in the story more now than i did before.
what is different about how you see him now?
i used to think he was just in the way of the children playing. now i see he was tired and still tried to help them.
reading the same story later in life can make a different person in it important to you. the words can stay the same while what you know about life changes.
i do not want to say my first reading was wrong.
you do not have to. the first reading gave you one way into the story. now you have another way to understand it.
help me write that in a few sentences, but do not add the name of the book.
i read this book as a child and liked the parts about the children. reading it again, i think more about their father. i can now see how tired he was and how he still tried to help them.
can i keep both ideas instead of choosing one as the right way?
yes. you can remember what you liked before and also enjoy what you understand now.
what if i read it again next year and think about someone else?
then the story may give you something else to think about. that does not take away what you found in it before.
only give me a warm last sentence.
it sounds like a book that has stayed with you.
my friend sent me a photo of a tree by her new home. she said it is the first thing she sees in the morning. i want a warm reply.
that sounds like a good thing to see in the morning. i hope your new place is starting to feel like home.
can you say that without saying you saw the photo? i have only told you about it.
you could write: that sounds like a good thing to see in the morning. i hope your new place is starting to feel like home.
she says it does, but she still wants something from the old street in her life.
a new place can feel like home while there are still things to miss from the old one. both feelings can be true.
write a reply in my voice.
i am happy the new place is starting to feel like home. you can still miss the old street too.
would asking what she wants from the old place be kind, or would it make her sad?
it could give her room to talk if she wants to. you can ask without choosing what she must feel.
make the question short and open.
what do you miss most about the old street?
she says the people, not the road itself. what could i say next?
it sounds like the people made that place important to you.
now only give the reply about the new home and old street again.
i am happy the new place is starting to feel like home. you can still miss the old street too.
what is different between i need to go and i want to go?
need to can give something that has to be done. want to gives what you would like. sometimes both can be true.
give me an example where i want to stay but need to go.
i want to stay and talk, but i need to go to work.
now an example where i need to stay but want to go.
i want to go for a walk, but i need to stay home with my child.
does that say the person never likes being with the child?
no. it gives two things about that moment. a wish for a walk does not say the person never enjoys time with the child.
can you make both needs and wants about the same thing?
i need to eat, and i want to have lunch now.
why did you use need with i but needs in she needs?
with i, use need. with she in that kind of sentence, use needs.
now turn she needs to leave into a question.
does she need to leave?
why did needs change back?
after does in that question, use need.
just give the question and a short yes answer.
does she need to leave? yes, she does.
write a story about a family listening to a radio while making dinner. one person wants quiet for a while, and the family listens to that request.

a family had the radio on while making dinner. the father was getting vegetables ready, and the mother was putting cups on the table. their daughter came in with a book and sat down near the window. after a few minutes, she asked whether they could turn the radio off for a little while. she had been in a busy place all day and wanted some quiet. her father turned it off, and the room was quiet. they kept making dinner, but now they could hear the cups being put down and the water in the kitchen. later, the daughter asked about a story her mother had started telling the day before. they talked until the food was ready. the evening had not needed a large change. one small request had changed how the room felt.
did the daughter say music was always wrong?
no. she asked for quiet for a little while after a busy day.
what did the family do after turning the radio off?
they kept making dinner and later talked about a story.
can you make the story about my family using we?
we had the radio on while making dinner. one person asked for some quiet after a busy day, so we turned it off for a while. we kept cooking and later talked together until the food was ready.
what did that shorter story leave out?
it left out which person was getting vegetables ready, who was putting cups down, and the book near the window.
only give the request the daughter could say.
could we turn the radio off for a little while?
when i read a sentence with a word i do not know, should i stop the whole page?
not always. you can first look at the words around it and ask whether you understand the general idea. if the word is important, you can ask about it.
what if i understand what the person does but not what object they use?
then you can ask what object the word is about, or use the rest of the sentence to see what kind of thing it might be.
here is a simple example. the child put the object on the table. what can i know without knowing the object?
you know a child put something on a table. you do not know what the thing was.
can you say it was a book because children often read?
no. that would add a specific object the sentence did not give.
now i tell you the object was a cup. does that change what the child did?
no. the child still put it on the table. you have made the object more specific.
write the sentence with cup.
the child put the cup on the table.
what question would help if i did not know where the table was?
where was the table?
does every question need to be answered before i understand the basic sentence?
no. you can understand what the person did and the objects in the sentence without every detail about the whole room.
i took a different road home today. it was longer, but i liked seeing a part of the town i usually miss.
what did you see that made the longer way good for you?
a little shop with flowers near the door. i did not buy anything, but i stopped to look.
that sounds like a small new part of the town you can remember, even without buying something.
my brother asked why i would choose a longer walk when i could get home in less time.
you can say you wanted to see something different, not only get home as fast as possible.
write that as a short reply.
i took the longer road because i wanted to see a different part of town.
can you add that i had enough time today, but not make it a rule for every day?
i had enough time today, so i took the longer road to see a different part of town.
what if tomorrow i choose the short road?
then you are making a different choice for a different day. a long walk you liked today does not make the short road wrong tomorrow.
just reply to the part about flowers now.
it sounds like the flowers gave you a good reason to stop for a moment.
i need to go now. no more questions.
goodbye. i hope the rest of your day goes well.
my neighbor gave me soup in a container. i washed it after eating and want to return it. write a short thank you.
thank you for the soup. i have washed the container. when would be a good time to bring it back?
why did you not say i enjoyed it?
because you did not tell me whether you enjoyed the soup. i can thank someone for giving it without choosing that feeling for you.
now i add that it was very good. write the whole message again, a little more warm.
thank you for the soup. it was very good. i have washed the container and would like to bring it back when it works for you.
if i say i will bring back the soup, is that the same?
no. you ate the soup. you are bringing back the container, not the food that was inside it.
what if some soup is left and i want to keep it until tomorrow?
then you can say the container is still being used, if that is true, and ask whether returning it later is okay.
write that without saying i already washed it.
thank you for the soup. i still have some left for tomorrow. would it be okay to bring the container back after that?
why did you leave out washed?
because the new message keeps soup in the container. saying it was already washed would not go with that meaning.
only give the question about bringing it later.
would it be okay to bring the container back after tomorrow?
is i read because i was waiting the same as i was waiting because i read?
no. in the first, waiting is the reason you read. in the other, reading is given as the reason you were waiting.
can the first mean i had time to read while waiting for a train?
yes. you could say: i read because i was waiting for the train and had some time.
what if i only say while instead of because?
i read while waiting for the train gives the two things at the same time, without making one the reason for the other.
now give a clear because example with a cup.
i washed the cup because it needed washing.
can you give only the part with because?
because it needed washing.
can i change which part goes first and keep the same reason?
because the cup needed washing, i washed it.
what stayed the same?
the cup needed washing, and that was the reason you washed it. changing the order of those parts did not change the reason.
now only give a while example with the cup and another person.
i washed the cup while my sister read.
my friend asked if i want to come over after a busy week. i like seeing her, but i do not want a late night.
you can say you would like to visit and ask whether a short visit early in the evening would work.
write that in my voice without saying i do not like her house.
i would like to see you. would a short visit early in the evening work for you?
she says yes, but another friend may come too. i thought it would be just the two of us.
then you can ask about the plan before choosing. do you want help saying that?
yes. do not make it sound like i hate the other friend.
i thought it would be a quiet visit with just us. do you know whether it will be a larger group?
she says only three people, and i am happy with that.
then you can keep the short visit and say the small group works for you.
write the reply.
that works for me. i would still like to keep it a short visit because i am tired after the week.
does that say i will leave at a specific hour?
no. it gives a short visit as the plan, but does not choose an hour.
now ask about the start time only.
what time would you like me to come?
make a sentence saying the girl finished the page before her father called.
the girl had finished the page before her father called.
now make it about the page not being finished yet.
the girl had not finished the page when her father called.
did the call happen before or after the finish in the new sentence?
at the time of the call, the finish had not happened yet. the sentence does not tell us when she finished later.
what if she never finished?
that is also possible. the sentence only says she had not finished at the time of the call.
can you make it clear she finished after talking?
the girl had not finished the page when her father called, but she finished it after they talked.
now tell it in her own voice.
i had not finished the page when my father called, but i finished it after we talked.
why did they become we?
because she is now one of the people talking. in her own words, we is about her and her father.
change the sentence to a question about whether she had finished before the call.
had she finished the page before her father called?
answer no, using a short answer.
no, she had not.
i talked to my new neighbor for the first time today. we were both waiting near the front door and started talking about the weather.
what was it like to have that first conversation?
short, but nice. she asked how long i had lived there. i had seen her before but never said more than hello.
then today gave you a little more time to know each other, even if it was only a short talk.
can you help me write two sentences about it without saying we are best friends now?
i had a short conversation with my new neighbor today while we were waiting near the front door. it was nice to talk for more than a short hello.
give me just the sentence about more than hello.
it was nice to talk for more than a short hello.
is that enough for the memory, or should i make it a larger story?
it can be enough. a small conversation can be important to you without a large story around it.
give just the part about important to me.
a small conversation can be important to you.
give a kind reply to what i first said.
it sounds like a good first conversation with your neighbor.
now say goodbye without asking what she is called.
goodbye. i hope your evening goes well.
write a story about two children making one picture for school. one should draw and the other should write words. make it clear both helped.

two children sat at a table with a large piece of paper. their teacher had asked them to make a picture about the town. one child liked drawing, and the other liked writing. they talked about what to put on the page before starting. the first drew the school, a road, and a tree by the library. the other wrote simple words near each place so people could understand what they were looking at. when there was not enough space for a word near the tree, they moved it together to a clear part of the paper. at the end, they looked at the whole picture, and each wrote a name on it. one had done most of the drawing, but both had helped make the work clear.
give me only the sentence about each child writing a name.
at the end, they looked at the whole picture, and each wrote a name on it.
who wrote the words near the places?
the child who liked writing.
did the child who drew do all the work?
no. one child drew, and the other wrote words to help people understand the picture.
can you make the story in our voice as if we are the two children?
we made one picture about the town. one of us drew the places, and the other wrote words near them. we chose where things should go together and both helped make the picture clear.
does both mean the teacher too?
not in that sentence. both is about the two children making the picture.
just give the sentence saying both helped, without saying each did the same thing.
we did different parts, but both helped make the picture clear.
my sister said she might visit after work. i told my mother she will come. now i think i made it sound too sure.
yes. might visit leaves the choice open, while will come sounds more sure. you can give your mother the words your sister used.
write the message with might.
she said she might visit after work. it is not chosen for sure yet.
what if my mother has already made dinner for her?
then it may be useful to tell her soon so she knows the plan is still open. you can also ask your sister whether she has chosen yet.
write a short question to my sister. do not make it sound like she was wrong, because i changed the meaning in my own message.
have you chosen whether you will visit after work?
if my sister says she has not chosen, what do i tell my mother?
she has not chosen yet, so the visit is still only possible.
now she says yes, i will come. can i use will then?
yes. she has now said the visit is her plan.
write that as a short message to my mother.
she has chosen to come after work.
does that give the hour?
no. after work still does not give a specific hour.
i found an old garment i had when i was young. it is too small for me now, but i do not want to lose it.
what does it help you remember?
a visit with my grandmother. i do not remember every part of the day, but i remember sitting by her while she told me a story.
the old garment helps you remember time with your grandmother, even though you do not use it now.
say that in my voice.
the old garment helps me remember a visit with my grandmother, even though i do not use it now.
do i have to keep every old object if it helps me remember something?
no. you can choose which objects are important to you. one object having a memory does not make a rule about keeping everything.
what if i want a picture of it but not the whole object?
that can be a choice too. you can keep a picture if that gives you the part of the memory you want to save.
can you choose for me?
i can help you think about the choices, but you know what the object and memory mean to you.
just give me a short sentence i could tell myself.
i can choose what helps me remember without keeping every object.
now give a kind reply to the part about my grandmother.
it sounds like a warm memory of sitting with your grandmother.
give me an example with she has written, but do not make it about my family.
she has written a letter.
now use they.
they have written a letter.
why have instead of has?
with they in this example, use have. with she, use has.
can the group have written one letter together?
yes. they have written a letter can be one letter made by the group.
what if each person wrote a different one?
then make that clear: each person has written a letter.
now make it a question about the group.
have they written a letter?
answer that they have not yet.
no, they have not written a letter yet.
does yet say they never will?
no. it leaves writing later possible.
can you tell me my parents have not written a letter from that example?
no. you asked for grammar examples, not a fact about your parents.
only give the first sentence again.
she has written a letter.
help me write about a picture. a woman is standing by a house with a child near her. i do not know when the picture was taken.
a woman is standing by a house, with a child near her.
can you make it two sentences without choosing weather or time?
a woman is standing by a house. a child is near her.
what if i add that the woman is my aunt?
my aunt is standing by a house. a child is near her.
can you say the child is her son?
not unless you give that information. a child near her does not have to be her son.
i know it is my cousin, but i do not know whether the house was theirs.
then you can say my aunt and cousin are standing near a house, without saying it was their house.
write it in two sentences using only those facts.
my aunt is standing by a house. my cousin is near her.
can you add that it was a happy day?
not as a fact if you do not know that. you can say how you feel looking at the picture, if you want to give that feeling.
i feel happy seeing them together.
you could add: i feel happy when i look at them together in this picture.
now only give that last sentence.
i feel happy when i look at them together in this picture.
i had a short break at work and just looked out of the window. i did not check my phone or read anything.
what was that quiet time like for you?
at first i felt i should be doing something useful. then i liked not having another thing to finish.
rest does not always need a task inside it. a few minutes without another thing to finish can still be useful to you.
i do not want to make rest another thing i must always do right.
you do not have to. you can simply say you had a quiet break today and liked it.
i mean do not make it a test. write two sentences in my voice.
i had a short break at work and looked out of the window. i liked having a few minutes without another thing to finish.
does that mean i hate my work?
no. you can like a break and still like your work.
say that with you can like a break.
you can like a break and still like your work.
now give a warm reply without asking what i saw outside.
it sounds like the quiet break gave you something you needed today.
just goodbye now.
goodbye. i hope the rest of your day goes well.
write a story about someone visiting a cousin on two different days. the first time they do not have much to say, but the next visit is more easy.

a woman visited her cousin after not seeing him for a long time. they sat at the table with tea and asked simple questions about work and home. she wanted to talk more, but she did not know where to begin. near the end of the visit, he showed her a drawing he had made of the town where they grew up. she remembered the tree near their old school and told him about it. on the next visit, she brought an old photo of the same place. they put the drawing and photo on the table and talked about what had changed. the pictures gave them a place to start. they still had more to learn about the life each of them had now, but the conversation felt more easy.
give just the sentence about the life each had now.
they still had more to learn about the life each of them had now, but the conversation felt more easy.
what helped the next visit?
the drawing and photo gave them a place and a memory to talk about together.
does the first quiet visit mean they did not care about each other?
no. having little to say at first does not tell us that. the story says she wanted to talk more but did not know where to begin.
now give the first visit in her own voice, just two sentences.
i visited my cousin after not seeing him for a long time. i wanted to talk more, but i did not know where to begin.
what did she bring on the next visit?
an old photo of the town where they grew up.
can you join these ideas with not only: she read the story. she wrote about it.
she not only read the story but also wrote about it.
does not only mean she did not read?
no. she did read. not only puts that fact together with another thing she did.
now use a visit and a meal.
we not only visited our aunt but also had lunch with her.
can both parts happen on the same day?
yes. that sentence can be about one visit with lunch, though it does not give the day by itself.
what if i want the last part to be about reading together after lunch?
we not only had lunch with our aunt but also read together after the meal.
does the sentence say whose voice people heard as they read?
no. read together does not say whether one person read to the group or everyone read quietly.
give me only that answer about the group.
read together does not say whether one person read to the group or everyone read quietly.
now only give the first example with the story again.
she not only read the story but also wrote about it.
that answered my question. i do not need more examples right now.
okay. we can stop there.
can you say that in a warm way without adding a new question?
it is good that the answer helped. we can leave it there for now.
do not say you have feelings like a person. keep it about the answer helping.
it is good that the answer helped. we can leave it there for now.
now just wish me a good day.
i hope you have a good day.
make it a goodbye too.
goodbye. i hope you have a good day.
only one word now.
goodbye.
